title: OKR-linked dependency risk lane and triage runbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Create an operational runbook and lightweight UI lane that explicitly ties active OKRs and initiative priorities to live inter-team dependencies, surfaces risk scores, and prescribes an agreed triage cadence.

Why: Roadmap churn is often caused by misaligned priorities across teams where downstream dependencies do not reflect rolling OKR priorities. By making OKR ownership visible in the dependency lifecycle and standardizing a triage flow we reduce surprise escalations, improve cutover predictability, and provide measurable mitigation windows for high-impact items.

Scope:
- Data model: map OKRs -> initiatives -> dependent tickets (cross-team). OKR tags will be canonical and pulled from our planning workspace.
- Risk scoring: combine (a) criticality to OKR (direct/indirect), (b) slack in schedule (buffer days), (c) owner confidence (self-reported), and (d) historical volatility (past delays).
- UI lane: a condensed view in the roadmap board and the Roadmap Health dashboard showing top N OKR-linked high-risk dependencies, their owners, and next action.
- Runbook: triage steps, SLA for acknowledgement, escalation ladder (PM -> ENG lead -> Security/Infra as needed), and template communication snippets.
- Integrations: Linear (source of truth tickets), Confluence (PRD links), GitHub (PR status), and Observability (latency/cost dashboards) for context.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Canonical mapping exists for at least 3 company OKRs to initiatives and their cross-team dependencies.
2) Risk score algorithm implemented as a job that updates dependency records nightly.
3) Roadmap Health dashboard surfaces top 25 OKR-linked high-risk dependencies with links to owners and evidence.
4) Runbook published to Confluence with triage SLAs and signed off by Eng, Design, Security, and Infra leads.
5) One pilot cutover using the lane/process documented and retro collected.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- 40% reduction in unplanned cutover delays for OKR-critical initiatives during pilot teams.
- Mean time to acknowledge a flagged dependency < 8 hours.
- 80% of flagged items have an explicit mitigation plan within 72 hours.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 0–1: Finalize data contract and risk formula with stakeholders (PM, ENG, Design, Security, Infra).
- Week 2: Ship nightly scoring job and API to annotate Linear tickets with risk tags.
- Week 3: Deliver Roadmap Health UI lane mock and iterate with Design.
- Week 4: Publish runbook and run tabletop with pilot teams.
- Week 5–8: Pilot + iterate; instrument metrics and retro.

Risks & mitigations:
- Incomplete OKR tagging in upstream systems -> mitigation: add lightweight adoptability checklist and auto-suggest logic.
- Noise from low-confidence self-reports -> mitigation: weight historical volatility and require evidence fields for high-impact items.
- Cross-team buy-in -> mitigation: require sign-off from each function for pilot and include on-call rotation in runbook.

- Runbook draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcd-OKR-Dep-Runbook

Notes on non-goals:
- Not building a full workflow engine; this is a visibility + triage pattern with light automation.
- Not replacing team-specific release processes; only augmenting cross-team signposts and SLAs.
